bio: Research Overview Research Background Education Publications Contact Us Dr. Gerard T. Berry’s primary interest is in carbohydrate metabolism, and galactosemia. Dr. Berry’s basic science and clinical research efforts are focused on hereditary galactosemia, and inositol metabolism in the brain, particularly during fetal development. He has employed in vivo isotope kinetic studies using [13C]-labeled sugars and mass spectrometry to dissect whole body galactose metabolism and breath testing to establish genotype-phenotype relationships in patients with galactosemia due to galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase (GALT) deficiency. He is working with investigators in the USA and Europe to establish an international database of patients with galactosemia.
